The observer is **not ready for the authorized fresh calibration**. No game,
browser, server, production build or live attempt was started. The final offline
pass retains the named close blue/gold actors and prevents duplicate
actor/pickup IDs, but still misses visible blue enemies and labels disconnected
player lobes and HUD contours as actors. Per instruction, these failures end
this task at a bounded offline result. No production defect is established.

## Exact identities and boundaries

## Observer-only implementation

All work is ignored under this directory. `original-tools/` contains byte copies
of the supplied observer tools, not edits to E. The copied original launcher and
controller are provenance only and must not be run: they still name the old
ports/evidence directory. No runnable live replacement controller is claimed.

`observer.py` is a new screenshot-only prototype:

- It fits the field from image edges first, removes only the measured rim, and
  requires local stroke/body evidence. It has no maximum actor-size cap.
- It fills original cyan contours without closing/dilating every contour across
  gaps. That morphological closing initially fused the close northern blue
  actor onto the player; removing it recovered the separate object.
- Distinct gold fill, with a one-stroke antialias bridge, retains gold actors
  whose cyan outline is open. This is material-based segmentation, not a
  blanket minimum-mask or maximum-size workaround.
- The filled component covering the camera anchor and a one-pixel stroke halo
  replace the62.5px exclusion disk. Independent nearby components retain IDs.
  This is an incomplete silhouette estimate: disconnected mounted lobes and
  overlaps remain unresolved. `selfReliable` stays false and blocks live use.
- Actor/pickup/unknown labels share one object partition; an ID has exactly one
  label. Pale blue actor/pickup ambiguity remains unknown. Pink projectile/status
  material conflicts remain unknown. Candidate disappearance is not collection.
- The old bottom-strip exclusion is gone, retaining the gold actor near y411.
  Top-panel masks are still fixed image rectangles; actual changing HUD coverage
  and merged actor/HUD contours are **not resolved**.
- PNG coordinates are normalized to the logical550x450 stage with the exact

`policy.mjs` is a pure, checked safety-policy prototype, **not integrated live
control**. Nearby/fallback collection use the same pickup/unknown/actor partition
and swept-path ambiguity check. Wall reserve accounts for measured canvas speed,
braking, silhouette extent, fit error and oldest-image capture-to-input age plus
the next observation budget. World-to-canvas and CSS-to-canvas conversions are
separate. No motion constants were blindly halved or newly claimed calibrated.

The policy explicitly records calibration, combat/collection/search, intentional
departure, arriving and stopped states. A destination map change enters arriving
and preserves the intentional direction; it never declares arrival on a map
change or blind three-second wait. **Independent public arrival evidence is
unvalidated and completion is deliberately disabled**, another live blocker.

input.body:
## Summary

Friendly seekers could inherit a same-ID replacement target, while Sappers aimed at the current avatar instead of retaining their source target. Target loss also replayed callbacks and movement that the source disables. This preserves object ownership, parent-space aiming and the separate Setup/Run phases together.

```text
friendly seeker
  retain target object while physically contained
  reacquire first raw candidate when detached
  convert actual parent and cached detail to global
  failed Setup: queue callback, never start motion
  failure inside Run: finish its movement tail once
Sapper
  retain steering/contact target
  refresh damage/shield avatar separately in base Run
  return contact selects refreshed avatar
  removed emitter returns zero without writing rotation
```

Third dependent layer above PR #141, following PR #140. Hold master until five layers are assembled on the final PR and its combined current-head Actions/review gate passes. Existing stack/** Vercel suppression remains; no deployment retry or provider changes.

## Evidence

- **Before:** All nine added source-contract regressions fail on dad4de6: same-ID replacement, missing/stale array membership, two Point-aiming cases, failed Setup versus in-Run target loss, separate Sapper target/avatar lifetime and removed emitter behavior.
  **After:** All pass, including the retained old target on failed reacquisition and one gated explosion/hit callback. Converter supplies its actual selected object. Existing assertions remain; isolated fixtures now set complete target/return-state pairs and actual camera/actor parents.
- **Before:** Raw local coordinates skipped display Point conversion, and current-world lookup conflated independently retained objects.
  **After:** Formatting, TypeScript and976 unit tests /8,728 assertions pass. Final production build SGofqOmsFRu5W1kJLevpv and all16 affected mock/supplied-art browser cases pass with zero skips, flaky results or page errors. Native homing/special-projectile galleries were inspected; owned servers stopped. All519 source/test/tool digests match the final pre-build manifest. Commands, ten original source/pcode identities and phase limits are recorded in docs/projectile-target-ownership-reference.md.
- An initial private build found unused copied helper files with invalid relocated imports. Those copies were removed; no compiler option, required spec or assertion was weakened. Final verification repeated the complete scoped browser suite after preserving the failed-acquisition reference.
- The observer-only prototype failed its offline gate and did not launch a fresh game. That evidence remains tied to its historical build; it establishes neither a production defect nor ordinary boss/win completion.

## Merge Danger
